read.thesis: Regulated utility reports 2025 EPS of $6.31 and guides 2026 to $6.55–$6.80, with 4.5 GW of signed data-center ESAs and a $103B capex plan raised $6B; the growth case rests on load ramp from late 2027.

capex.quote: our capital plan is increasing as we progress further into the generation build cycle

triggers.label: Signed data-center ESAs 3.0 → 4.5 GW
triggers.quote: now have approximately four and a half gigawatts of data center load secured under ESAs

triggers.label: Capex plan up 18% to $103B
triggers.quote: represents an increase of 18% versus our prior plan

triggers.label: 2026 EPS guide $6.55–$6.80
triggers.quote: we set our adjusted EPS guidance range at $6.55 to $6.80 for 2026

triggers.label: Equity need ~35% of capex, $10B 2027–30
triggers.quote: Our financing plan includes $10 billion of equity in the 2027 to 2030 timeframe

guidance.quote: we set our adjusted EPS guidance range at $6.55 to $6.80 for 2026
extending our 5% to 7% long-term EPS growth rate through 2030
We are forecasting 2026 FFO to debt of approximately 14%
our plan assumes normal weather and retail sales growth of 1.5% to 2% in 2026

prior_guidance_check.metric: Tennessee and Florida transactions earnings neutral
prior_guidance_check.quote: Consistent with prior guidance, we expect the Tennessee and Florida transactions to be earnings neutral

red_flags.label: Rate case affordability pushback
red_flags.quote: a lot of stakeholders are kind of watching the case

red_flags.label: Equity dilution 35% of capex
red_flags.quote: This represents approximately 35% equity funding of the capital plan

red_flags.label: Rate base vs EPS gap (9.6% vs 5-7%)
red_flags.quote: The capital plan's 9.6% gross rate base CAGR would be 8.8% if minority interest in Florida is netted out

evasions.quote: We are still compiling those costs
